properties.title: Enhancing context-aware SARS disorder management: a proposed multi-agent simulation framework with machine learning and bio-sensor data integration

properties.source_path: Papers/001_2026_Enhancing context-aware SARS disorder management a proposed multi-agent simulation framework with machine learning and bio-sensor data integratio.pdf
properties.version_basis: Published article PDF; version identified by SHA-256 because no preprint or revision ID was assessed.

properties.description: Multi-agent NetLogo and ProbLog simulation plus WEKA comparison of five classifiers on a synthetic dataset, with an external MIMIC-III evaluation.
properties.independent_study_claim: single study; no overlap with other registry records assessed

properties.description: Proposed context-aware framework combining sensor and context input, ontology conversion, Bayesian belief network and rule engine, agent-based simulation and ML classifiers
properties.implementation_stage: simulation described and executed per authors; code not released

properties.responsibility: data input, ontology conversion and preprocessing (imputation, Min-Max scaling, smoothing)
NetLogo agent state and tick-based context update with ProbLog rules and Bayesian belief network
Normal versus SARS-risk classification readout with probability thresholds mapped to low, moderate and high alert levels

properties.population: generic respiratory distress, explicitly not a COVID-19 diagnostic system
properties.decision: whether to alert or notify clinical staff
properties.autonomy: alert states described as clinician-in-the-loop support; simulation also dispatches doctor and ambulance agents

properties.description: Synthetic simulation set of 1,000 virtual patients with 120 physiological records each; about 60% Normal and 40% SARS-risk
Described extract from UOL Teaching Hospital (up to 300 patients, 20 sensor types); role in the reported experiments is unclear
PhysioNet MIMIC-III Clinical Database used for external validation; version, cohort and label definition not stated
Virtual patients of the simulation dataset; split unit (record or patient) not stated
MIMIC-III subset used for external validation; selection criteria not stated
Repeated stratified 70/30 train-test splits on the simulation dataset in WEKA (Table 8)
External validation of the classifiers on MIMIC-III; results given in narrative and Figure 7 only
Qualitative demonstration of ProbLog multi-agent reasoning (Figure 5) and NetLogo agent behavior (Figure 6); no quantitative endpoint

properties.algorithm: SMO (support vector machine trained by sequential minimal optimization)

assertions.rationale: Authors state that no recurrent or state-space longitudinal model is used. Ticks and rules carry time implicitly. Classifiers are trained per record and are not transition models. The NetLogo update code is not shown, so a hidden fitted update cannot be fully excluded (see review queue).
No action pathway into any transition or prediction.
Random agent movement is described (Table 3) but no stochastic health-state transition is defined.
Rule-based clinical thresholds, modular context rules and a Bayesian network constrain inference. These are symbolic structure, not physiological equations.

legacy_cells.B: Enhancing context-aware SARS disorder management: a proposed multi-agent simulation framework with machine learning and bio-sensor data integration
legacy_cells.C: Abdullah; Zulaikha Fatima; Nida Hafeez; Muhammad Ateeb Ather; Rolando Quintero Tellez; Grigori Sidorov; Carlos Guzmán Sánchez-Mejorada; Miguel Jesús Torres Ruiz
legacy_cells.I: 001_2026_Enhancing context-aware SARS disorder management a proposed multi-agent simulation framework with machine learning and bio-sensor data integratio.pdf
legacy_cells.O: SARS disorder (generic acute severe respiratory distress condition; not COVID-19)
legacy_cells.S: Whether monitoring data indicate Normal versus SARS-risk and should trigger an alert or clinical-staff notification.
legacy_cells.T: Synthetic simulation population of 1,000 virtual patients with 120 physiological records each; external validation on de-identified MIMIC-III ICU data.
legacy_cells.V: Whether to alert or notify clinical staff, and the resulting risk-alert level.
legacy_cells.AI: Physiological signals (heart rate; ECG-derived features; body temperature; systolic and diastolic blood pressure; oxygen saturation); patient history/context; environmental room temperature
legacy_cells.AN: Forward-fill for time-consistent signals; mean imputation for isolated missing entries.
legacy_cells.BN: Rule-based thresholds and Bayesian-network reasoning over physiological, environmental, and contextual variables.
legacy_cells.BS: Normal/SARS-risk class probabilities mapped to low-, moderate-, and high-risk alert levels.
legacy_cells.BT: Machine-learning classifiers for Normal/SARS-risk classification; probability thresholds map outputs to alert levels.
legacy_cells.DB: Patient, doctor, and sensor agents; environmental patch agents.
legacy_cells.DN: Synthetic simulation dataset; PhysioNet MIMIC-III Clinical Database
legacy_cells.DQ: 1,000 virtual patients (120 records each) in the simulation dataset; the hospital dataset description separately says up to 300 patients.
legacy_cells.EL: The authors report weak discrimination / low MCC for Naïve Bayes and difficulty handling imbalanced classes.
legacy_cells.EM: Risk-threshold alert levels and clinician-in-the-loop decision support.
legacy_cells.EO: Simulation inputs were synthetically generated and anonymized; the external clinical database was fully de-identified.
legacy_cells.EP: Clinician-in-the-loop decision support; alerts are described as support, not automated diagnoses.
legacy_cells.ER: Institutional ethical approval was stated to be unnecessary because the study used synthetic/anonymized data and fully de-identified external data.
legacy_cells.FL: Sensor and patient-context inputs → ontology/context conversion → Bayesian Belief Network and rule engine with classifier outputs → thresholded risk alerts and notifications; no demonstrated learned patient-transition model or planner.
legacy_cells.FM: The authors propose a context-aware multi-agent simulation integrating biosensor/context information, probabilistic reasoning, and machine-learning classifiers for generic severe respiratory-distress monitoring.
legacy_cells.FN: The authors report Logistic Regression accuracy 0.744 ± 0.018, precision 0.748 ± 0.021, recall 0.744 ± 0.019, F1 0.743 ± 0.020, MCC 0.530 ± 0.027, ROC-AUC 0.820 ± 0.015, and PR-AUC 0.827 ± 0.017 on repeated splits; on MIMIC-III they report accuracy 88.7% and ROC-AUC 0.91.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors state that explicit longitudinal disease-progression learning was not implemented; operational factors such as sensor noise, communication latency, heterogeneous sensor reliability, and workflow integration were outside validation scope. They also identify class imbalance and scalability across real-life environments as constraints.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work includes explicit temporal learning for long-term trajectories, advanced or hybrid models, real-time context adaptation, wearable devices, personalized regimes, long-term follow-up, and clinical validation.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors claim gaps in integration of probabilistic reasoning with context-aware systems, comparative ML evaluation, healthcare multi-agent simulation, biosensor/context integration, and simulation-based framework validation.
legacy_cells.FR: Tick-based agent updates and classifier results do not establish a learned/hybrid patient world model: the paper reports no future-state rollout metrics, specified intervention-conditioned patient predictions, causal identification, planning results, or prospective clinical evaluation. MIMIC-III validates classifiers, not the full end-to-end agent framework.
legacy_cells.FT: Keep tick-based context/alert simulation distinct from validated patient-dynamics modelling; its probabilistic alert thresholds and clinician hand-off are reusable as a monitoring interface, not as evidence of intervention-conditioned rollouts.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted PDF text, pp. 1–20: title/abstract and article metadata; introduction and contribution; literature review and research gap; Methods §§3.1–3.6 (data, preprocessing, platform, classifiers, agent simulation, evaluation); Results and Tables 1–8; discussion, limitations, conclusion, data availability and ethics statements; references. Form-feed page breaks were retained. Table 8's extracted layout was inspected; its row alignment is ambiguous. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I were left untouched because the PDF did not directly contradict the prefilled bibliographic/source fields. The article describes tick-based agent updates and probabilistic alerts, but its reported evaluations are classification results, not learned/hybrid patient-dynamics rollouts or planning. Dataset counts conflict: the hospital dataset is described as up to 300 patients, while the synthetic simulation dataset is described as 1,000 virtual patients with 120 records each. Table 8's extracted row alignment is ambiguous; quantitative findings were taken from the prose summary on PDF p. 16. The full-agent framework was assessed in simulation; MIMIC-III validation concerns the classifiers. Evidence QA: 18/63 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (28.6%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 63 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 0 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: The NetLogo update code is not shown, so absence of a learned transition rests on author statements and the described rules.
Legacy workbook columns were reviewed selectively; the remainder stay imported-only (see coverage sidecar).
Review is by one model pass with a second skeptical read; no independent human review or replication.

All seven figures and eight tables now covered together with prior checks. Figure2 uses five layer labels whereas prose/Figure3 organize four layers; these remain schematic design descriptions, not an implemented learned transition or autonomous clinical evaluation. Referenced papers were not retrieved.
